items.heading: Ask Five Engineering Students What
items.text: Ask five engineering students what a PSU job means, and you usually get one answer: "step score, then apply to a few companies, then wait." That picture is incomplete.

items.heading: Before Choosing a Specific Psu,
items.text: Before choosing a specific PSU, understand that you are choosing between two structurally different recruitment processes.

items.heading: Over 70 Public Sector Undertakings
items.text: Over 70 public sector undertakings across sectors like oil and gas, power, mining, and heavy engineering use step scores as their primary or first-stage recruitment filter instead of running a separate written exam of their own. This is the door most engineering students hear about first, and it genuinely is the fastest single-exam path into a strong-paying, stable PSU role for branches where step is a well-established recruitment channel.

rows: IOCL, ONGC, NTPC, Coal India, BHEL, GAIL, Power Grid, SAIL, BPCL, HPCL
Most of the highest-profile step-recruiting names sit in this tier, which is exactly why their cutoffs run steep.
NALCO, RVNL, Container Corporation, NMDC, BEL
Still step-based in most cycles for engineering roles, with somewhat more reachable vacancy-to-applicant ratios than the top Maharatna names.
BEML, defence R&D bodies like DRDO and BARC, several state-level and category II Miniratna companies
Recruitment mode varies more here, some use step, some run their own written exam, so check the specific notification rather than assuming a pattern.
